issue.title: Monadic operations of `optional` and `expected` drop the cv-qualification of `T`

discussion.p:
The resolution of LWG (adopted in Kona) changed all occurrences of `value()` in to *val, and of `**this` in to val. The intention was not to change the meaning, just avoid the non-freestanding `value()` function, and avoid ADL that would be caused by using `**this`.
LWG then changed the exposition-only member of `optional` to

blockquote.pre: union { remove_cv_t<T> val; };

discussion.p:
following LWG for `expected`, and changed *val to val.
However, because val drops the cv-qualifiers of `T`, in the non-const overloads such as and_then(F&&) & the type of val is remove_cv_t<T>&, whereas the type of `value()` was T&. This means the callable can modify a const contained value:

This was ill-formed in C++23. The rvalue overloads have the same problem (std::move(val) is remove_cv_t<T>&& rather than T&&), as does volatile T.
Using `operator*()` instead of val restores the type that `value()` had, is freestanding, and does not perform ADL.

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) &; template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) const &;

blockquote.p:
-1- Let `U` be invoke_result_t<F, decltype((val)operator*())>.
-2- Mandates: remove_cvref_t<U> is a specialization of `optional`.
-3- Effects: Equivalent to:

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) &&; template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) const &&;

blockquote.p:
-4- Let `U` be invoke_result_t<F, decltype(std::move(valoperator*()))>.
-5- Mandates: remove_cvref_t<U> is a specialization of `optional`.
-6- Effects: Equivalent to:

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) &; template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) const &;

blockquote.p:
-7- Let `U` be remove_cv_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype((val)operator*())>>.
-8- Mandates: `U` is a valid contained type for `optional`. The declaration

blockquote.pre: U u(invoke(std::forward<F>(f), valoperator*()));

blockquote.p:
is well-formed for some invented variable `u`.
[Note 1: There is no requirement that `U` is movable (). — end note]
-9- Returns: If `*this` contains a value, an optional<U> object whose contained value is direct-non-list-initialized with invoke(std::forward<F>(f), valoperator*()); otherwise, optional<U>().

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) &&; template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) const &&;

blockquote.p:
-10- Let `U` be remove_cv_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(std::move(valoperator*()))>>.
-11- Mandates: `U` is a valid contained type for `optional`. The declaration

blockquote.pre: U u(invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(valoperator*())));

blockquote.p:
is well-formed for some invented variable `u`.
[Note 2: There is no requirement that U is movable (). — end note]
-12- Returns: If `*this` contains a value, an optional<U> object whose contained value is direct-non-list- initialized with invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(valoperator*())); otherwise, optional<U>().

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) &; template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) const &;

blockquote.p:
-1- Let `U` be remove_cvref_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype((val)operator*())>>.
-2- Constraints: is_constructible_v<E, decltype(error())> is `true`.
-3- Mandates: `U` is a specialization of `expected` and is_same_v<typename U::error_type, E> is `true`.
-4- Effects: Equivalent to:

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) &&; template<class F> constexpr auto and_then(F&& f) const &&;

blockquote.p:
-5- Let `U` be remove_cvref_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(std::move(valoperator*()))>>.
-6- Constraints: is_constructible_v<E, decltype(std::move(error()))> is `true`.
-7- Mandates: `U` is a specialization of `expected` and is_same_v<typename U::error_type, E> is `true`.
-8- Effects: Equivalent to:

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto or_else(F&& f) &; template<class F> constexpr auto or_else(F&& f) const &;

blockquote.p:
-9- Let `G` be remove_cvref_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(error())>>.
-10- Constraints: is_constructible_v<T, decltype((val)operator*())> is `true`.
-11- Mandates: `G` is a specialization of `expected` and is_same_v<typename G::value_type, T> is `true`.
-12- Effects: Equivalent to:

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto or_else(F&& f) &&; template<class F> constexpr auto or_else(F&& f) const &&;

blockquote.p:
-13- Let `G` be remove_cvref_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(std::move(error()))>>.
-14- Constraints: is_constructible_v<T, decltype(std::move(valoperator*()))> is `true`.
-15- Mandates: `G` is a specialization of `expected` and is_same_v<typename G::value_type, T> is `true`.
-16- Effects: Equivalent to:

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) &; template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) const &;

blockquote.p:
-17- Let `U` be remove_cv_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype((val)operator*())>>.
-18- Constraints: is_constructible_v<E, decltype(error())> is `true`.
-19- Mandates: `U` is a valid value type for `expected`. If is_void_v<U> is `false`, the declaration

blockquote.pre: U u(invoke(std::forward<F>(f), valoperator*()));

li.p: (20.1) — If `has_value()` is `false`, returns expected<U, E>(unexpect, error()).

(20.2) — Otherwise, if is_void_v<U> is `false`, returns an expected<U, E> object whose has_val member is `true` and val member is direct-non-list-initialized with invoke(std::forward<F>(f), valoperator*()).
(20.3) — Otherwise, evaluates invoke(std::forward<F>(f), valoperator*()) and then returns expected<U, E>().

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) &&; template<class F> constexpr auto transform(F&& f) const &&;

blockquote.p:
-21- Let `U` be remove_cv_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(std::move(valoperator*()))>>.
-22- Constraints: is_constructible_v<E, decltype(std::move(error()))> is `true`.
-23- Mandates: `U` is a valid value type for `expected`. If is_void_v<U> is `false`, the declaration

blockquote.pre: U u(invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(valoperator*())));

li.p: (24.1) — If `has_value()` is `false`, returns expected<U, E>(unexpect, std::move(error())).

(24.2) — Otherwise, if is_void_v<U> is `false`, returns an expected<U, E> object whose has_val member is `true` and val member is direct-non-list-initialized with invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(valoperator*())).
(24.3) — Otherwise, evaluates invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(valoperator*())) and then returns expected<U, E>().

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto transform_error(F&& f) &; template<class F> constexpr auto transform_error(F&& f) const &;

blockquote.p:
-25- Let `G` be remove_cv_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(error())>>.
-26- Constraints: is_constructible_v<T, decltype((val)operator*())> is `true`.
-27- Mandates: `G` is a valid template argument for `unexpected` () and the declaration

blockquote.pre: G g(invoke(std::forward<F>(f), error()));

blockquote.p:
is well-formed.
-28- Returns: If `has_value()` is `true`, expected<T, G>(in_place, valoperator*()); otherwise, an expected<T, G> object whose has_val member is `false` and unex member is direct-non-list-initialized with invoke(std::forward<F>(f), error()).

blockquote.pre: template<class F> constexpr auto transform_error(F&& f) &&; template<class F> constexpr auto transform_error(F&& f) const &&;

blockquote.p:
-29- Let `G` be remove_cv_t<invoke_result_t<F, decltype(std::move(error()))>>.
-30- Constraints: is_constructible_v<T, decltype(std::move(valoperator*()))> is `true`.
-31- Mandates: `G` is a valid template argument for `unexpected` () and the declaration

blockquote.pre: G g(invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(error())));

blockquote.p:
is well-formed.
-32- Returns: If `has_value()` is `true`, expected<T, G>(in_place, std::move(valoperator*())); otherwise, an expected<T, G> object whose has_val member is `false` and unex member is direct-non-list-initialized with invoke(std::forward<F>(f), std::move(error())).
